title: Thorn and Sigil Revisited
premise: Freya Underhill poisons herself daily so the crown can eat safely, a trade that has taught her every hidden road and whispered secret in the Thornfell mountains. When the old gods stir and begin answering the desperate prayers of smallfolk, Freya learns she is the last living bearer of the Underhill sigil—a bloodline bound to the dragon-fire that once sealed the gods away—and that the queen's spymaster intends to harvest her blood to reignite that ancient war. Torn between the court that uses her and the mountain folk who claim her, Freya must choose whether to feed the flame or let it gutter out, carrying a secret that could save or doom both worlds. In the end she burns the sigil into the last dragon's heart rather than her own, freeing the gods to be merely gods—and finally belonging to no crown at all.
about_author: Noor Whitlock is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade feeding mountain trail crews and collecting their ghost stories. They write fantasy about people who feed others for a living, and the quiet costs of being indispensable.

chapters.title: The Taster's Portion
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She swallows poison for the queen's table, catalogs the symptoms, and slips home through a smuggler's pass. Establishes her invisibility and her meticulous, survivalist mind. Emotional beat: weary pride in a trade nobody thanks her for.

chapters.title: Bread at the Crossroads
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A starving village woman leaves an offering at a forgotten shrine and the bread vanishes before Freya's eyes. Freya tells herself it was an animal. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in her rational world.

chapters.title: The Queen's Long Table
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At court she tastes a dish that makes her sigil-shaped birthmark burn. The spymaster, Lord Corvane, watches her too closely. Emotional beat: the chill of realizing she has been noticed.

chapters.title: What the Mountains Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She visits her grandmother's abandoned croft and finds the Underhill sigil carved over the hearth, matching her birthmark. Emotional beat: inheritance as a weight she never asked to carry.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The spymaster confirms Freya's bloodline through old census rolls and begins grooming her trust with small mercies. Emotional beat: predatory patience disguised as warmth.

chapters.title: Prayers with Teeth
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Smallfolk miracles spread through the Thornfell villages—wells sweetened, fevers broken—each answered with a price. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Dragon POV (the last dragon, Emberwake, dreaming beneath the mountain). The dragon senses the gods waking and its own fire failing. Emotional beat: ancient exhaustion, a keeper outliving its purpose.

chapters.title: A Taster's Network
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She uses smuggler contacts to map where prayers are being answered and finds the pattern points at the old sealed shrine beneath Thornfell keep. Emotional beat: her invisibility becomes an advantage at last.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Apprentice
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She takes on an orphan boy, Wick, as an assistant, teaching him herb-lore; he becomes the first person she's chosen to protect. Emotional beat: belonging offered, cautiously.

chapters.title: Blood and Honey
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He tests Freya with a poisoned dish meant to force her bloodmark to flare, confirming the sigil responds to her. Emotional beat: the trap closing with a smile.

chapters.title: The Shrine Below
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She descends into the sealed shrine and finds the gods' prison—a wall of fused dragon-glass—and her own family name on the seal. Emotional beat: the secret she must now carry made flesh.

chapters.title: Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She begins lying to the court about what she tastes, buying time to investigate. Wick covers for her. Emotional beat: guilt and exhilaration of first betrayal.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers
chapters.summary: Old god POV (the Whisperer beneath the shrine). It has been listening for centuries and has found a voice in the desperate. Emotional beat: hunger dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Queen Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Queen's POV. The queen, dying and desperate, learns of the sigil and orders Corvane to secure Freya 'gently.' Emotional beat: a ruler's fear wearing the mask of necessity.

chapters.title: Run, Taster
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Warned by a sympathetic servant, Freya flees court with Wick through the smuggler roads she knows best. Emotional beat: flight as freedom and loss at once.

chapters.title: The Hearthfolk
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Mountain villagers shelter her, calling her 'sigil-bearer' and asking for miracles she can't perform. Emotional beat: belonging that feels like a burden.

chapters.title: Corvane's Hounds
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. His hunters close in; he burns a village that harbored Freya to flush her out. Emotional beat: the corruption of power, methodical and unashamed.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She returns to the burned village and buries the dead; her rage awakens something in the dragon-glass she carries—a shard taken from the shrine. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Emberwake Wakes
chapters.summary: Dragon POV. The shard's call drags Emberwake half-awake; it mistakes Freya for the first Underhill. Emotional beat: two lonely ancient-and-modern creatures recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Price of Miracles
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The Whisperer offers her a deal: her blood to open the seal, in exchange for the villagers' safety. She refuses; a child is taken. Emotional beat: the horror that refusal has costs too.

chapters.title: Wick's Choice
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. The boy tries to trade himself to the god in Freya's place and barely escapes, learning how the god feeds on devotion. Emotional beat: love learning its limits.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Captured by mountain rebels, Corvane reveals the crown's plan: use Freya's blood to control the gods as weapons of war. Emotional beat: villainy with a coherent, chilling logic.

chapters.title: The Rebel Table
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The mountain factions meet; Freya cooks for them for the first time as an act of care rather than duty, and they begin to trust her. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not assigned.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Knew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In her grandmother's letters she learns the Underhills were seal-keepers, not sacrifices—the sigil can close the prison as well as open it. Emotional beat: hope with a terrible price attached.

chapters.title: The Queen's Last Feast
chapters.summary: Queen's POV. The dying queen hosts a feast and demands Corvane deliver Freya before the solstice; Corvane begins to consider replacing her. Emotional beat: power devouring its own.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Corvane's soldiers ambush the rebels at the river crossing; Freya uses her knowledge of the smuggler roads to save them, revealing herself publicly as the sigil-bearer. Emotional beat: invisibility surrendered.

chapters.title: The Shard Sings
chapters.summary: Dragon POV. Emberwake rises fully, shattering a mountain pass, and comes to Freya, kneeling. The world sees its first dragon in three hundred years. Emotional beat: awe and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Riders and Ruin
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. With Emberwake, the rebels strike Corvane's supply lines; war fever grips the lowlands, and the queen declares the mountains in rebellion. Emotional beat: momentum she can no longer steer.

chapters.title: The Whisperer's Church
chapters.summary: Old god POV. The Whisperer builds a following among the war's desperate, feeding on prayers for victory. Emotional beat: corruption of faith into fuel.

chapters.title: Freya's Bargain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She offers the god a counter-deal: her blood to open the seal if it releases the child and stops feeding on prayers. The god agrees—and she plans to betray it. Emotional beat: the taster's oldest skill, swallowing the poison.

chapters.title: Corvane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The queen dies; Corvane seizes the regency and marches on the shrine with an army and a blood-iron cage built for Freya. Emotional beat: ambition crowned.

chapters.title: The Long Road Down
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She and Wick travel to the shrine ahead of the army, saying goodbyes along the way. Emotional beat: the quiet before the storm, love made explicit at last.

chapters.title: Siege of the Deep Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Corvane's army and the rebels collide at the shrine entrance while Freya slips below. Emotional beat: chaos, and one small figure moving against it.

chapters.title: The Opened Seal
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She opens the prison as bargained; the gods begin to pour out, and the Whisperer reneges immediately, seizing her. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, despair bottoming out.

chapters.title: Corvane's Harvest
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He arrives to take the sigil-blood for himself, killing the god's avatar in the process—power devouring power. Emotional beat: hubris at its peak.

chapters.title: Emberwake's Fire
chapters.summary: Dragon POV. Emberwake breaks into the shrine, dying, and offers its last fire to Freya. Emotional beat: a keeper's final gift, and the choice of a lifetime.

chapters.title: The Last Tasting
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax: instead of pouring her blood into the war, Freya burns the sigil into Emberwake's heart with the dragon's own fire, forging a new seal that lets the gods out as diminished, mortal-ish beings—no longer weapons. Corvane, reaching for the flame, is consumed. Emotional beat: sacrifice redefined—she gives up the inheritance, not herself.

chapters.title: Ashes and Bread
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aftermath: the mountain folk and lowlanders begin uneasy talks; Freya bakes bread for the funeral tables, her mark now just a scar. Emotional beat: grief and ordinary care.

chapters.title: A New Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The diminished gods answer small, honest prayers without price; villagers ask Freya to be their priestess and she declines, offering instead to teach. Emotional beat: belonging chosen freely.

chapters.title: Thornfell Green
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, closing. One year on, Freya runs a school for tasters and healers with Wick at her side; Emberwake's egg—found warm in the shrine—begins to crack. Emotional beat: the future, guarded and hopeful, finally hers.
